findings.issue: The `app_settings` table declares columns `[id, quiet_hours_start, quiet_hours_end, notify_quota, conversion_window_days]` — there is no `email_subject_template` or `email_body_template` column. Yet `POST /admin/settings` requestShape includes `"email_subject_template": "text"`, and the `send-restock-email` capability lists `"email subject template"` as a dataNeed. The admin contract writes a setting that has no backing column; the notify capability consumes a value that nothing stores. This is phantom storage: the coding agent will either fabricate a column name or silently drop the template feature.
findings.fix: Add `email_subject_template` (role: text, nullable: false) and `email_body_template` (role: text, nullable: false) columns to `app_settings`, and add `email_body_template` to the `POST /admin/settings` requestShape.

findings.issue: The `restock_events` dedup key is `["inventory_item_external_id", "detected_at"]`, and the column's purpose states it holds "the timestamp of the inventory_levels/update webhook." However, the `inventory_levels/update` payloadBindings bind only `inventory_item_id`, `available`, and `location_id` — no timestamp field is bound from the payload. If `detected_at` is set to `NOW()` at insertion time, two re-deliveries of the same webhook will each get a different wall-clock value and the dedup key will not fire. The coding agent has no declared source for the timestamp value that the dedup actually depends on.
findings.fix: Add a `signalField` of "inventory level updated at" to the `inventory_levels/update` trigger with a payloadBinding to `payloadPath: "updated_at"` (present on the payload), rename the `restock_events` column accordingly, and use that bound value — not `NOW()` — as the dedup timestamp.

findings.issue: The spec states `statusField` is "RESERVED for binding a column to a non-null stateMachine." The only declared `stateMachine` in the plan is bound to `item_availability_snapshots.availability_status`. Yet `restock_events`, `notification_batches`, and `notification_records` all declare a non-null `statusField: "status"` with no corresponding stateMachine. These are internal application workflow lifecycles (correctly excluded from a stateMachine per spec), so their `statusField` should be `null`; the `usesWorkflow` flag on the owning capabilities already binds the workflow helper for those columns.
findings.fix: Set `statusField: null` on `restock_events`, `notification_batches`, and `notification_records`; the `usesWorkflow: true` flags on `detect-restock`, `dispatch-notification-batch`, and `record-notification-outcome` are the correct and sufficient binding for the workflow helper.
